title: Does the hillside's rock ever read as stone, or is the procedural slope-blend a ceiling to accept?
body: Five real rounds — three on colour/value, two on height/relief, one full order of magnitude apart in amplitude — with real measured movement on every lever and zero movement in a blind critic's verdict across all five.
clears: The owner looks at shots/hillside/dome-overview.png and either accepts the read, or says in their own words what's actually wrong.

title: Is grandpas-house-route.png's “flanking” read worth further iteration, or a placement-density limit to accept?
body: Five rounds fixed genuine mechanisms (clump straddling, stray placement, oversized clump radius); two rounds that added density made the same frame measurably worse, for a now-understood reason.
clears: The owner looks at grandpas-house-route.png and says it's fine, or what's actually wrong, in their own words.

title: The square-convergence “unmotivated dark patch” is identified but not fixed — same open question as the route above
body: Direct pixel measurement found the real cause: pure-path pixels average luma 130, pure-grass pixels average luma 67 — ordinary material contrast, not a rendering defect. Fixing it trades against the path's own feathered-edge design.
clears: The owner accepts the current read or names the tradeoff they want; the fix may also close the route entry above.

title: Does the creature roster clear a Palworld-level appeal bar, or does it need to?
body: Four blind-judge rounds called all three previewed starters “an asset preview, not a hero character portrait.” The only lever is a roster-wide material/lighting pass — no new meshes are permitted at any credit balance.
clears: The owner says whether a roster-wide pass is worth commissioning, and if so, whose scope it joins.

title: NP1-geometry — no real hair/accessory geometry exists, and generating one is foreclosed
body: Checked directly: villager_female/male/grunt are each one fused mesh, no separable hair/accessory node — same limitation as trainer/Grandpa/Warden. The only fix is another Meshy generation, which D23/D24 forbid for this purpose.
clears: The owner accepts the placeholder-primitive look as permanent, or names a non-Meshy source (a CC0 pack) for modular hair/accessory parts.

title: ASSET_LEDGER.md's licence claim is false
body: The ledger states everything in the build is CC0 1.0. It isn't — the Meshy-generated creatures and the Plumberry Plains pack are not CC0.
clears: The owner supplies the correct licence wording.
